4th Period.workingNow: Making a copy of a page on your site, linking it from your index page, and starting your two paragraphs.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: A persuasive 'How I Think We Should Use AI' article live on your portfolio site — your argued position on the best way to use AI, backed by this week's research, plus at least one image — pushed to GitHub Pages by Sunday night.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can build and link a new page on my site and write two paragraphs about one AI issue so that a visitor can read the background and then my opinion.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.13 — Create prototypes using structured code, organized into separate linked pages, to fulfill a design requirement.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.11 — Supporting own opinions and evaluating others' opinions in speaking and writing.
agenda: Quick overview: today's plan + the topic list (3 min)
I do: copy a page, link it on index, add <h1> and <p> (10 min)
You do: pick your topic, find one source to link (10 min)
You do: write both paragraphs — background, then opinion (23 min)
Exit Ticket: paste your live page URL (2 min)
4th Period.connections: Tuesday you defined what AI is; yesterday you learned what it does with whatever you type into it. Today you pick the one AI issue you actually have an opinion about and start the page where you'll argue it — background and a real source first, then how you feel about it. That page is due live on your site Sunday night.

6th Period.workingNow: Getting your mechanic and aesthetic papers back, and working out how one of your rules could create the feeling you picked.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: MDA framework notes (Mechanics, Dynamics, Aesthetics) + a one-page Game Design Plan for your SchoolAI game, shared with Ms. Herrick by Sunday night.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can explain how one of my mechanics creates the feeling I chose so that my rules and my aesthetic work together instead of against each other.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.13 — Design and iteratively develop computational artifacts for practical intent, personal expression, or to address a societal issue.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.1 — Exchanging information and ideas with others through collaborative discussions.
agenda: Quick overview + get your two papers back (4 min)
I do: how one rule creates one feeling (10 min)
We do: trace a shared game's rule to its feeling (8 min)
You do: match your mechanics to your aesthetic, in pairs (20 min)
Exit Ticket: one mechanic + the feeling it makes (5 min)
6th Period.connections: Tuesday you picked your mechanics and yesterday you picked your aesthetic — today you have both papers in front of you and connect them: which rule actually produces that feeling? Tomorrow you turn that thinking into a written design proposal, and that proposal is what we build your game's state machine from next week.
